source_read: PDF, pp. 1946–1949 (all 4 pages): text read in full; Table 1 (p. 1947) and Figure 1 (p. 1948; panels A and C also on higher-resolution crops of the rendered page) checked on rendered pages; all 18 overall AAPCs in Table 1 recomputed from the printed segments; supplement not available.

Abstract (p. 1946) and Results 1st paragraph (p. 1947). The sex split and mean age describe the 2023 deaths: 9,559 + 25,296 = 34,855.
Table 1 (rendered p. 1947); the segments reproduce the printed AAPC of 18.49 (recomputed).
Table 1 opioid rows; the fentanyl and other-opioid AAPCs (40.57 and 13.20) reproduce from their segments. The 76.24% sentence is in the part of the Results 2nd paragraph printed on p. 1948.

key_findings.correction: First sentence confirmed (58/730 = 7.95%, 274/2,666 = 10.28%, 41,583/73,379 = 56.67%). Second sentence: Figure 1A does not show the share. It plots crude rates per 100,000 of methamphetamine-involved deaths overall, with fentanyl and with other opioids (rendered page and crop). Suggested: 'No count or share of methamphetamine-involved deaths that also involved opioids is printed; Figure 1A plots their crude rates overall, with fentanyl and with other opioids (values not extracted).' Read from the figure for information only, 2023: about 6.9 per 100,000 with fentanyl and about 1.0 with other opioids against 10.4 overall; the overlap between the two opioid series is not given.

key_findings.note: p. 1948, Results 3rd paragraph; all four shares recomputed from their counts.

reporting_issues.note: 34,855 against 35,126 (0.8% apart) and 29,449 against 29,692; the 'final against provisional' explanation is plausible but is the card's inference, as worded.
Recomputed (segment APCs weighted by segment length): women, methamphetamine, 18.61; men, cocaine, 8.54, exactly the two printed values swapped. All other 16 overall AAPCs reproduce to two decimals.
Recomputed: with 1999–2006, 2006–2012 and 2012–2023 the AAPC is 9.63, as printed.

The sentence (Discussion, 1st paragraph) can also be read as each drug separately (33.19% and 28.06%, each roughly one-third) with 'nearly half' respectively for methamphetamine among American Indian or Alaska Native people (44.50%) and for cocaine among Black people (48.47%); so it is ambiguous rather than wrong. The consequence (no combined share; do not cite one) stands.

risk_of_bias.note: JBI prevalence fits a registry count. Overall moderate agreed; the domain judgments are reasonable for a coded proxy whose definition is in an unread supplement, with a provisional final year.

risk_of_bias_domains.note: See missed: the 2021–2023 segment rests on three yearly values.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor agreed, but one of the card's points is not a gap: the abstract's statement that methamphetamine-involved deaths were highest among American Indian or Alaska Native people also holds for rates, since Figure 1C shows their crude rate far above the other groups (about 32 per 100,000 in 2023 against about 12 for White people, read from the rendered figure). Suggest deleting that sentence from 'claimed', and changing 'conflates' to 'is ambiguous' for the one-third sentence (reporting issue 4).

missed: The 2021–2023 slowdown (3.39% a year, 0.24 to 6.76, p = 0.04; Table 1) is a Joinpoint segment fitted to three yearly values (2021, 2022 and the provisional 2023), so its estimate is fragile beyond the provisional-data point the card already makes; the same holds for every 2021–2023 segment in Table 1.
